wiki_text: Under the 'Atlantic LNG 2.0' restructuring, the four-train Point Fortin facility was consolidated into a single unitised entity. The new ownership structure for the consolidated facility took effect on 1 October 2024 with Shell and bp each holding 47.15% and the National Gas Company of Trinidad and Tobago (NGC) holding 5.7%; from 2 May 2027 the structure shifts to Shell 45% / bp 45% / NGC 10%. Train 1, idled since 2020 on feed-gas shortages, was decoupled from the facility; bp confirmed in March 2025 that Train 1 will be permanently decommissioned, and reporting in January 2026 indicated decommissioning would begin in Q4 2026 (Train 1 being the least-efficient unit). Shell's July 2024 FID on the Manatee gas field had been viewed as possible upside for the facility, but Manatee start-up slipped toward 2028.
